newsitem.title: ITALY: Disney's first cruise ship launched in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Disney's first cruise ship launched in Italy.

text.p: The "Disney Magic", Walt Disney Co's first cruise ship, was officially launched at a ceremony on Tuesday at Italian state shipbuilder Fincantieri's Venice-Marghera shipyard.

Esta Rodney, wife of Disney Cruise Line President Art Rodney, broke a traditional bottle of champagne over the ship's bow at the technical launch before the 85,000 gross tonne vessel was floated out of a building dock to a fitting-out pier.
Trieste-based Fincantieri said the Disney Magic, the first of two 2,400 passenger capacity, cartoon-themed sister ships it is building for Disney, will be delivered in early 1998.

In a few days, also at Marghera, Fincantieri will lay down the first block of the keel of the second purpose-designed ship, the Disney Wonder, due to be delivered at the end of 1998. Cruise industry experts estimate Disney spent over $300 million to build each ship in its debut into the cruise industry.
The Disney Magic is the largest passenger ship ever designed and built to transit the Panama Canal.
Fincantieri said that in an exceptional piece of naval surgery the two sections of the vessel were built separately at its Venice-Marghera and Ancona yards and then welded together at Marghera.

Walt Disney Co began accepting reservations for its fledgling cruise line last September. The Disney Magic will operate between Port Canaveral, Florida, where Disney is building a passenger terminal, and Nassau port and Castaway Cay, Disney's private island in the Bahamas.

On May 22 at its Monfalcone yard near Trieste, Fincantieri will float out the Grand Princess -- at 109,000 gross tonnes the largest passenger ship ever built and flagship-to-be of the P&O Group's Princess Cruises fleet. It is due for handover in spring 1998.
The world's previous biggest cruise liner, the 101,000 GT Carnival Destiny, also built by Fincantieri at Monfalcone, was handed over to Carnival Corp's Carnival Cruise Lines last October.
